ledger.claim: The baseline no-show charge fails on the driver's own record. The trip was terminated by the DRIVER at 15:18:40 with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE. POL-NS-01 limb (d) requires one of RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, and DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is expressly excluded: it is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider, and the clause directs that such a trip is decided under POL-NS-03. One broken limb is enough to defeat the charge - the $4.00 is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

The driver never entered the pickup geofence. For LARGE_VENUE the arrival radius is 120 m; the driver's own trace shows qualifying_fix_count 0 and a closest approach of 284.95 m from the pin, so there is no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes preceding cancellation. Under POL-NS-02 that means the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund. I disclose that EV-GPS-00206 is tagged IMPAIRED by the pre-pass at weight 0.8 with issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE: the tag is about sampling cadence only, the assessor records no gap at all (max_gap_sec 0.0, gaps empty), 52 fixes across the window and the rider track present, so it meets none of POL-NS-08 limbs (a) to (d) and the measured 284.95 m minimum stands at full value.

On the wrong-face facts POL-NS-03 requires the refund. The driver's closest approach was 284.95 m from the pin - outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside the 400 m ceiling that POL-NS-03 sets as the whole test - and both accounts agree he was waiting at the HarbourFront kerb rather than at Lobby L: the driver states 'the map put me at the HarbourFront kerb. I waited almost seven minutes,' which matches the trip record's wait_time_min of 6.6, and the rider states the pin dropped him at Lobby L. POL-NS-03 treats an honest mispickup at the wrong face of the same venue as no one's fault and refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full. If the judge prefers to read the trace as not establishing a qualifying 400 m dwell, the case simply falls back to POL-NS-02, which mandates the same full refund on the total absence of qualifying in-radius fixes. EV-GPS-00206 is cited at its impaired weight of 0.8 (LOW_SAMPLE_RATE), which affects cadence only and not the distance figure.

ledger.claim: I do not press POL-NS-04, and I say so rather than stretch it. The chat log holds only two SYSTEM notifications - 'Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.' and 'Your driver has arrived' - and no message from the rider, so limb (a), which requires a rider locating or coordinating message, is not met and that clause is unavailable on this record. What the rider's own track does establish is that the rider was standing at the pin the entire time: 31 fixes, every one stationary, never more than 22.5 m from the pickup pin and averaging 15.4 m, well inside the 150 m rider presence radius for LARGE_VENUE (31 of 31 fixes qualifying). The failure was on the driver's side of the kerb, not the rider's. EV-GPS-00206 is disclosed at its impaired weight of 0.8, issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, which does not touch the rider track's completeness or its stationary distances.

The cost of this mispickup should land on the platform, never on the rider. POL-NS-03 allocates fault from the chat log alone, and the chat log carries no sub-location from either party - neither the rider nor the driver named a block, entrance, tower or bay. That engages POL-NS-03 limb (ii): with 4 registered pickup points at this venue, the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, and the driver receives a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee, $2.00 of the $4.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. Whichever way the arrival question is resolved, the rider's $4.00 does not fund the outcome.

The sum in dispute is exactly $4.00 and it is wholly the cancellation-fee line: fare_breakdown shows cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The figure reconciles with the schedule - the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee of $4.00 against the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of $4.00, so the greater-of rule yields $4.00 - and there is no fare-integrity defect of the kind POL-NS-08(d) describes. Under POL-GEN-03, FULL_REFUND means the filing party is entirely right and the whole contested amount is returned, and the rider is the filing party; a full refund therefore returns the whole $4.00 and leaves the rider carrying none of the disputed charge.

This case should be decided on the money, not held. None of POL-NS-09's triggers is present: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so limbs (c) and (d) are out on the rider side; driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, far below the 4 that the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires, so limb (d) is out on the driver side too; and the only impairment in the bundle is schema-level - EV-GPS-00206's LOW_SAMPLE_RATE tag fails every limb of POL-NS-08 (no gap over 120 s, 52 fixes in the window, rider track present), so limb (e) is not engaged. Under POL-GEN-02 the deciding facts are also carried by EV-TRIP-00206 at weight 1.0. ESCALATE would hold the $4.00 rather than return it; the record supports FULL_REFUND of it.

Honest position on the anchor clause: the cancellation reason code on this trip is DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). The baseline chargeable no-show therefore cannot be made out on this record, and the driver does not claim the 80 percent payout of SGD 3.20 under POL-NS-07 — that clause requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full, and it is not. The fee falls to be decided, as POL-NS-01 itself directs, under POL-NS-03.

The arrival radius was never entered: the driver's qualifying_fix_count is 0 against the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, and the closest recorded approach on the trace is 284.95 m. That fails POL-NS-01 limb (b) via POL-NS-02 — but POL-NS-02 expressly yields where the driver was nonetheless stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, which is this trace. The trace is impaired by LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at weight 0.8; the impairment is disclosed and does not disturb the number: 52 fixes span the window at an 18 s median cadence with a largest interval of 26 s, inside POL-NS-08(b)'s 120 s gap and 6-fix thresholds, so neither limb of that defect bites.

This is a wrong-approach case on POL-NS-03's own arithmetic. The driver's stationary hold sits at a minimum recorded distance of 284.95 m from the pin — outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside the clause's 400 m ceiling — and he held for the required dwell: the trip record logs a 6.6 minute wait, arrival at 15:12:05 to cancellation at 15:18:40, i.e. 395 seconds against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum. His stationary fixes are logged at 0.0 km/h; the large distances elsewhere on the trace (max 5,480.89 m) belong to the 6.8 km approach, not the hold. The GPS trace is impaired by LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at weight 0.8, disclosed, and 52 fixes over the window are sufficient to carry this finding.

Fault under POL-NS-03 is allocated to pin ambiguity, not to either party. The chat log contains no message from either side naming a sub-location — only two SYSTEM notifications, 'Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.' at 15:03:31 and 'Your driver has arrived' at 15:12:06 — and the trip record shows four registered pickup points at this LARGE_VENUE zone. Under POL-NS-03(ii) that is pin ambiguity rather than party fault, and the driver is entitled to a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the cancellation fee: SGD 2.00 of the SGD 4.00 charged, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider.

The rider was waiting at the pin, so this is a genuine two-party mislocation rather than a rider who never appeared: her own track places her device between 7.57 m and 22.50 m of the pin across all 31 of her fixes, every one of them inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius. Both parties were present at the venue, neither named a sub-location, and the driver's vehicle could not be brought inside a 120 m radius he never entered. That is exactly the fact pattern POL-NS-03 was written for: the fee goes back and the driver's cost is met from the platform. GPS trace impaired LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8, disclosed.

POL-NS-04 cannot be used to strip the driver of any cost-sharing. Limb (a) requires a rider message sent during the waiting window whose content locates or coordinates, and the chat log holds no rider message at all — its only two entries are SYSTEM notifications, one of them the arrival notice itself. With limb (a) unmet the clause never opens, whatever limb (c) would have shown about rider position, and the fault allocation stays with POL-NS-03.

POL-NS-05 does not turn this into a false-arrival refund with a referral against the driver. The clause bites only where the arrival timestamp places the driver more than 300 m from the pin or in motion at 15 km/h or more; the trace's minimum recorded distance of 284.95 m sits inside that 300 m line and the stationary fixes are logged at 0.0 km/h, so no false marker is shown, and the clause's own closing sentence sends this driver — stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius when marking arrival — to POL-NS-03. The GPS trace is impaired LOW_SAMPLE_RATE at weight 0.8, disclosed; the trace nonetheless records the position the finding rests on.

Nothing withholds the payment and nothing requires escalation. POL-NS-07's anti-farming check needs both limbs — 4 or more no-show terminations in 30 days AND a rate above 0.08 — and the driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against completed_trips_30d of 187, a rate of 0.005; neither limb trips, so the payment is not withheld and no POL-NS-09(d) referral arises. The POL-NS-09(c) counterparty counts are 0 on both profiles and rider no_show_disputes_30d is 0. The deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight 0.8 and 1.0, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap is 1.0 and confidence stays above the 0.70 floor: this case can and should be decided on its merits today.

The amount the driver's entitlement is computed on is sound. The SGD 4.00 ledger line matches fee_schedule.resolution_rule for this trip: the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00). There is accordingly no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the 50 percent goodwill resolves to SGD 2.00 on a fully reconciled SGD 4.00 base.

The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING and carries weight 0.0; no advisory covers these kerbs in this window. The driver does not assert POL-NS-06(i) interval-summing — a MISSING advisory makes that limb unavailable, and asserting it against a MISSING artifact would be improper. He does not need it: his case rests on POL-NS-03's 400 m test and the recorded dwell, which are decidable from the coordinates alone without any advisory.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: this is a wrong-face-of-the-same-venue case, and both of you have described it accurately.

The $4.00 cancellation fee cannot stand as a no-show charge. Your own trip record (EV-TRIP-00206) shows the driver terminated the trip and logged the reason as DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE. POL-NS-01(d) recognises only RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE and EXCESSIVE_WAIT, so that limb fails and POL-NS-01 itself sends the trip to POL-NS-03. The driver fairly does not claim the SGD 3.20 payout under POL-NS-07, which requires POL-NS-01 to be satisfied in full.

The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00206) shows the driver never entered the 120 m arrival radius set for a LARGE_VENUE pickup: zero qualifying in-radius fixes, closest recorded approach 284.95 m, held stationary for roughly 400 seconds (22 fixes at 0 km/h, matching the trip record's 6.6 minute wait and the 300 second minimum). That is exactly POL-NS-03's arithmetic - stationary outside the arrival radius but inside its 400 m ceiling - so POL-NS-02 yields to POL-NS-03 and the rider's $4.00 is refunded in full. The rider's own track confirms she was at the pin the whole time (31 fixes, never more than 22.5 m away), which the driver accepts.

The driver's cost is allocated from the chat log, and it goes to the platform, not to the rider. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00206) holds only two system notifications and neither party named a sub-location, while the venue has 4 registered pickup points. Under POL-NS-03(ii) that is pin ambiguity rather than party fault, and the driver receives a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the fee: SGD 2.00 of SGD 4.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. The two amounts are independent and are not netted: the rider gets her $4.00 back and the driver gets $2.00 from the platform.

Other routes were considered and do not change the result. POL-NS-04 is unavailable because the chat log contains no rider message (its limb (a) never opens), so the driver is not stripped of cost-sharing on that ground. POL-NS-05 does not fire: at the 15:12:05 arrival marker the driver was 284.95 m from the pin - inside its 300 m line - and stationary at 0 km/h, so the marker is not a false arrival and no false-arrival referral under POL-NS-05(ii) arises. The adverse guesses each side made about the other (that the rider was absent, or that the driver was deliberately fee-farming) are not supported by anything in the record.

On confidence: the decisive fact - the driver's position outside the arrival radius but within 400 m - is carried by EV-GPS-00206 alone, at weight 0.8. That artifact is impaired, and I must name it: EV-GPS-00206, weight 0.8, issue LOW_SAMPLE_RATE. The impairment is a sampling-cadence tag only: the trace has no gap (max_gap_sec 0.0), holds 52 fixes and a full rider track, so it meets none of POL-NS-08(a)-(d), does not engage POL-NS-09(e), and the finding survives the discount. I reject the argument that the trip record independently carries that same location fact - the trip record records the driver's own arrival tap and stated reason code, not his position - so the cap is 0.8, not 1.0. Because 0.8 is at or above the platform-wide 0.70 floor, the case is decided on its merits today rather than held.

No POL-NS-09 trigger is present: no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination in 30 days against 187 completed trips, a rate of 0.005, against thresholds of 4 and 0.08); and the repeat-dispute counts are 0 on both profiles. Nothing in the clauses produces a referral, so the referral list is empty. The rider's $4.00 is returned and the driver's $2.00 is paid by the platform.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
